newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Seven killed in south Mogadishu fighting.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed in south Mogadishu fighting.

text.p: Gunmen loyal to rival south Mogadishu faction leaders Hussein Aideed and Ali Hassan Osman Atto killed seven people in fighting on Friday, witnesses said.
They said shooting broke out late on Thursday when three people were killed in a civilian vehicle and two militiamen were killed when a mine wrecked their "technical" battlewagon at a checkpoint.
The militiamen were from the Aideed faction, they added.
Both sides blamed the other for starting the fighting involving mortar and artillery fire. At least seven people were killed and 18 were wounded, witnesses said.

Muse Sudi Yalahow, the Moslem fundamentalist leader of Medina district who is allied with Osman Atto, blamed Aideeds faction for starting the fighting and said two people were killed and 11 wounded by mortar blasts in Medina on Friday.
A stray shell crashed into a vegetable market elsewhere in south Mogadishu and a mortar bomb exploded in a house, killing a man and wounding two people. Other civilian areas were also hit.
The south Mogadishu bloodshed followed the killing of 14 people in heavy fighting in northern Mogadishu on Wednesday between gunmen loyal to another faction chief and an Islamic leader.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991 and is divided by rival forces of which Ali Mahdis and Aideeds are widely considered the largest.
